claim: Many code generation errors stem from token-ranking mistakes at high-uncertainty decoding steps, where the correct token is present in the distribution but not top-ranked.
stance_target: token-level uncertainty is diagnostic of error-prone decoding steps, even if not well-calibrated as an expressed confidence signal
scope_conditions: LLM-based code generation, greedy decoding baseline
quoted_support: This paper presents an empirical study revealing that many generation errors stem from token ranking mistakes at high-uncertainty steps, where the correct token is present but not top-ranked.

claim: AdaDec, a lookahead-based uncertainty-guided decoding framework that pauses and reranks tokens at high-uncertainty steps, improves Pass@1 accuracy by up to 20.9 absolute percentage points over greedy decoding on code generation benchmarks.
stance_target: uncertainty signals can be turned into a downstream decoding ACTION with a measured accuracy payoff
quoted_support: Experiments on HumanEval+, MBPP+, and DevEval benchmarks show that AdaDec improves Pass@1 accuracy by up to 20.9% in absolute terms over greedy decoding.

claim: AdaDec consistently outperforms both Beam Search and the adaptive-decoding baseline AdapT, while maintaining efficiency through selective, uncertainty-triggered pausing rather than exhaustive search.
stance_target: selective/triggered use of uncertainty is more efficient than blanket search-based decoding strategies
scope_conditions: same three code benchmarks; comparison against Beam Search and AdapT baselines
quoted_support: it consistently outperforms both competitive baselines like Beam Search and state-of-the-art adaptive decoding methods such as AdapT, while maintaining high efficiency through selective, uncertainty-triggered pausing.

claim: AdaDec learns model-specific uncertainty thresholds rather than using a fixed universal threshold, implying that raw uncertainty scales differ across code LLMs and require per-model calibration for use as a decision trigger.
stance_target: uncertainty signal scale is model-dependent, a practical caveat for any prescriptive method built on it
scope_conditions: multiple code LLMs, per-model threshold learning
quoted_support: AdaDec learns model-specific uncertainty thresholds and applies a lookahead-based reranking strategy when uncertainty is high.

claim: AdaDec never reports the calibration quality (e.g., AUROC, ECE, Brier score) of the token-level uncertainty signal it uses as a trigger, treating uncertainty purely as a heuristic rather than a validated probability of correctness.
stance_target: gap: no calibration audit of the signal used for a real downstream action, leaving open whether a better-calibrated signal (e.g., sampling-based) would yield larger gains
scope_conditions: inferred from abstract; full paper not accessed
quoted_support: Motivated by these findings, we propose AdaDec, a lookahead-based uncertainty-guided adaptive decoding framework that integrates a token-level pause-then-rerank mechanism driven by token uncertainty.
